description:
Problem: make oracle-review-recover (scripts/oracle_review_recover.py) reruns failed oracle-review runs. When the pull request is not armed, it then closes and reopens it, which restarts the pull request's full CI; that happened on #3385 on 2026-10-24. With oracle-gate the only required oracle check, the target refreshes nothing that gates a merge. The required gate is refreshed with: gh workflow run oracle-gate.yml --ref develop -f pr=<number>. scripts/pr_rerun.py imports the module (import oracle_review_recover as recover) only for generic CLI and pull-request helpers; it does not call recover().

Outcome: the script, its tests and the Make target are gone. pr_rerun keeps its behavior, with the helpers it uses moved into it. Docs and help name the oracle-gate dispatch for gate refreshes and make pr-rerun for CI reruns.

Decision gates (stop and report if one fails):
1. List every symbol that pr_rerun.py, or any other importer, uses from oracle_review_recover. If anything beyond generic helpers is used (for example recover() or the close-and-reopen path), stop and re-plan.
2. Grep for oracle-review-recover and oracle_review_recover across the repository: Makefile, make/*.mk, docs, scripts, tests, CI and .claude/skills. Mirrored skill files cannot be hand-edited; if they reference the target, create a follow-up item for the skill catalog instead of editing the mirror.
3. Read tests/unit/scripts/test_check_makefile_inventory.py to see how public targets are pinned before removing the target.

Item guardrails: preserve make pr-rerun behavior (failed CI rerun, required-suite rerun, head-change, shared-head and retarget refusals) and its CLI. Do not add oracle-gate dispatch to pr_rerun. Delete the module and migrate its imports in the same commit. Leave decision-record history text that names the old target as history.

Common guardrails: work only in a linked worktree created by make worktree-create, after make agent-write-preflight; the primary clone is read-only. No SKIP or --no-verify, no stand-in approvals, no ruleset edits or bypasses, no raw gh pr merge. Close out with make pr-preflight, make pr-open, oracle SHIP on the exact head, then make pr-arm. Do not change oracle-gate's App binding (integration 5201041), the oracle decision rule, or the native review-thread-resolution requirement. Do not close and reopen, mass-rerun or rebase other pull requests. No explanatory comments or docstrings (COMMENT-POLICY-001). Every behavior change gets a test that fails on the previous code.
